doc.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: His clarinet equipment and the Hanon exercises
summary: He lists his Bari mouthpiece, Denman reeds, metal barrel and Yamaha clarinet, and says Hanon exercises can be swung.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You know we don’t usually ask technical questions, but we may have a few clarinet players who might ask you about your instrument and the odd looking barrel—
The odd looking barrel? Well let’s see from top to bottom this is my creation, this mouthpiece and it’s put out by Bari, they release it, Bari mouthpieces.

Yeah, right. They put out the BDF mouthpiece. John Denman, by the way, John Denman makes excellent clarinet reeds, he’s in Tucson, a fine clarinet player. Bob Wiban ligature, from Kansas, and this is a Accubore barrel, which is made of metal, not wood, so that it doesn’t change so much from different areas and climates. And it’s a Yamaha clarinet, and I’ve played Yamaha clarinets, what 24 years. This is about the best system I’ve worked out to play what I do in modern jazz.
Yeah you always try to get away from the agony. Well I’ll tell you those Hanon exercises will teach you about agony.
Can you swing ‘em too? © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
Well you actually can. I think unconsciously that’s why I chose them because they can lend themselves to lines that you would play in jazz.
